candidates.text:
this is probably all over your feed. But it’s a 7 month old video. 

why did it go viral now? 

since my Inbound Engineer post blew up 2 weeks ago I’ve had the pleasure of consulting with marketing teams of some well known companies, and some billion dollar ones that nobody knows (which is the problem) 

this is an example of a concept we’ve discussed called “script-based editing”

I’ve used it in the past to get clips over 1m views  

here’s how it works:
- start with video “hub content”
- pull up the transcript and put it on a Google doc
- run it through Claude to find a moment with one of the 10 storytelling ingredients (see below)
- edit the TRANSCRIPT into 130 words that would go viral if put on a text based platform like X 
- then edit the video to match that exact transcript 

storytelling ingredients: 
1. Social proof
2. Curiosity gap
3. Promised benefit
4. Odd numbers
5. Specific timeframe
6. Unique POV
7. Contrarian take 
8. Trend-jacking
9. Condense Effort
10. Experiment + Findings

this video with Tobi used 1, 3, 7, 6, and 9 

you don’t need a video editor to go viral. You need an Inbound Engineer

candidates.text:
people often ask, “who are the best KOLs?”

i think that is the wrong question

the better question is:

which KOL fits this goal, audience and stage of the campaign?

if the product is unknown, you need KOLs who can create awareness and hype

if people know the product but take no action, you need conversion-focused KOLs

if the product is difficult to understand, you need strong educators

if you want early adopters, you need alpha callers with a trusted audience

these are different jobs. treating every KOL the same usually leads to wasted budget and poor results

i have worked with hundreds of KOLs over the past two years at @Growgami. i have managed campaigns for top protocols and tier-one projects

i have seen the posts. more importantly, i have seen what happened behind them

reach does not always produce users

good content does not always create hype

strong conversion does not always come from the biggest account

the operator’s job is not to gather popular names

the job is to know who can produce the result that matters.

candidates.text:
building on top of “knowing which game to play”

- software like this is inherently, fundamentally on retention.

typical saas margins assume 70:30 (not sure how this gets affected with inference but yeah) 

and let’s assume a basic 1:3 (CAC to LTV) - it will be higher starting out and then reduce as u grow and hit colder audiences.

so a product that did 5m in revenue in a year with 70% margins will make 3.5mil gross, at 1:3 cac to ltv, that’s 1.6 mil in acquisition cost (everything included, not just ur ads)

[ note - in actuality, ltv is usually gross profit based, not total revenue and the 70% gross profit only covers cogs, not other meaning stuff, oh and im conflating ltv with annual revenue here] 

which leaves $1.9million in profit for the startup 

————

the game is - how do you eventually reach a place where most users retain, which gets you higher LTV and allows for higher CAC

CAC always gets more expensive as u grow, companies that can spend the most on acquisition eventually win, and those that can spend the most on acquisition are the ones that have the ltv and margins to do so.

which means for a saas - 

-> do everything you can to keep your core icp happy and retaining.

-> all marketing should find pockets of most profitable , highest retaining users and focus on getting more of them.

-> you should know the reason for every person leaving, especially if they were under ur core icp

-> do EVERYTHING in ur power to find whatever is common in ur best retaining users and implement it across everyone

(also why billion dollar companies are the ones with the highest amount of retention - crm, insurance etc)

if you’ve got a product that retains and is stable and has margins - u can literally fire all engineering if shit hits the fan, ramp acquisition, get more users, use upfront payment options for longer duration lock ins to bring cash upfront and solve ur cash flow issues.

(all notes to self)
